title: The War Room Map
synopsis: The Bohrok-Kaita form up while the family pulls Stacey out of school to help plan the next mission using a homemade map of Mata Nui. Walkie-talkies, warp pads, and a full battle strategy get laid out at a kitchen-table war meeting, assigning each Toa a village to defend and a set of krana to collect before the Toa head out.

title: Krana Hunt Begins
synopsis: The Toa fan out to collect krana from the Bohrok hive, trading them for masks and gear as they go. It's fast, easy work at first, with krana handed over almost politely, before the mission turns into a proper search through a nervous, unfamiliar hive.

title: Into the Hive
synopsis: Deeper in the hive, the krana collecting turns tense as the heroes admit they're scared without their usual masks and weapons. After rounding up the last krana from a reluctant Bohrok, the group finally reaches the temple, where something with scraper-like eyes descends from above.

title: The Spirit of Makuta
synopsis: Inside the temple, the Toa face down a weaker duplicate calling itself the evil spirit of Makuta, warning that if it's defeated this time it's gone from the earth for good. Masks get knocked off and swapped mid-fight, with Gali losing and reclaiming her shielding mask before the spirit falls.

title: The Infected Mask
synopsis: The spirit battle continues with a parade of mask swaps and half-finished special moves, including one hero admitting they don't even know what half their new masks do. The fight turns nasty when an infected mask gets slapped onto a hero's face, forcing them to rest it off in their case before the battle wraps up.

title: Speed, Levitation, and Little Bro
synopsis: New masks come out to play as one hero floats on the Kamui mask of levitation and another blazes through a super-speed attack. A short, snappy round of challengers takes their turn against Makuta, with a fair bit of teasing about whose little brother has to go first.

title: Tahu's Turn to Battle
synopsis: Tahu steps up to face Makuta one-on-one, trading masks and jabs about Makuta's suspiciously fresh 'surgery' and reddish eyes. New mask powers get discovered on the fly mid-battle, and the fight ends with a tease that something bigger, a Toa Kaita, is about to enter the picture.

title: Hiura and the Third Defeat
synopsis: The combined Toa Kaita Hiura, fused from Gali, Lewa, and Kopaka, dominates the fight against Makuta, blocking and countering attack after attack until Makuta is defeated for a third time. Afterward the heroes plan their next move: with no fuel for their canisters, they'll fly out using their masks along a route called the Trin-Chrom Bridge, teased for the next video as 'Escape from Mata Nui.' The tape keeps rolling past the sign-off, briefly catching what sounds like dialogue from an unrelated video or show playing in the background rather than any Super Family footage.

title: Static Between Scenes
synopsis: This stretch of tape doesn't belong to the Super Family at all: the camcorder's mic picked up dialogue from an unrelated video or television show playing somewhere in the background, following characters bargaining over keys and stolen trinkets. No toy battle footage or Super Family narration appears in this segment.

title: A Quiet Stretch of Tape
synopsis: This segment of the tape has no narration at all. A mostly silent stretch of stop-motion battle action, with no dialogue captured on this part of the recording.

title: The Ice Villager Joins the Fight
synopsis: Movie 5 opens with an announcer segment: Basil has left the Super Family, and Kopeka, an ice villager, is the newest recruit. The family gathers at Mata Nui, trades morning-routine banter, and worries after the Toa never returned from a scouting mission against the Bohrok. Sensing an "ultimate evil," the team rallies together, pooling their power into one final blast, and marches off to confront Makuta's lair.

title: Makuta's Obedient Form
synopsis: The heroes face down one of Makuta's "obedient forms" in a rapid-fire toy battle, trading elemental attacks, a shielding "block screen," and a climactic hyper beam. Between hits the kids narrate combo attacks and taunts until the enemy is finally declared knocked out, but Makuta vows there's more fighting to come.

title: Chrono Shields and Cheap Shots
synopsis: More back-and-forth trash talk with Makuta, who's accused of "getting bored" and hiding behind "chrono shielding," while new fighters Sheila and Agent Nine jump into the fray with blasters. The narration is heavy on taunts and repeated lines as the toy battle grinds on, action escalating into a climbing, chaotic scramble.

title: Crystal Beam Confusion
synopsis: The battle intensifies as the heroes deploy a crystal beam and a "super confusion" attack to try to knock out their foe, while enemies fire their most powerful blasts skyward in a repeated, over-the-top barrage. It ends on a twist: the villains claim to have defeated the whole Super Family, except for Dr. Senor and Stacey.

title: Earning Your Kanohi
synopsis: After a rough surgery scare, the heroes take a breather to meditate and dodge Makuta's confusion attack, trading jabs about who's actually "earned" their Kanohi mask yet. The action shifts to the Tohunga warriors joining the fray, masks flipping on and off as everyone gears up to battle the spirit of Makuta together.

title: The Invisible Crab and the Weather Witch
synopsis: A short, scrappy round of skirmishing sees one of the heroes deploy a mysterious "invisible crab" attack while the team debates whether it counts as their most powerful move. The water-elemental fighter, apparently tempted toward the evil side, is eventually blasted down and taken on by Stacy, who's warned that their foe can control the weather.

title: Makuta's Sons
synopsis: The battle rolls into an extended showdown where Makuta rallies with a grand speech about his eternal duty to "protect the universe," then bitterly reveals that his own sons have been destroyed in the fighting, naming them one by one. It ends with Makuta powering up through a mysterious "Powerball" for one last attack, which the heroes vow to block.

title: The Last Battle and a Tape from the Past
synopsis: Makuta falls for good, the Super Family celebrates, and the young director signs off, promising the next movie will be a battle-free Christmas special. But the tape doesn't stop rolling: it rolls into leftover footage from an old recorded broadcast, an unrelated Redwall TV segment about a warlord called Clooney the Scourge, heraldry, and a trivia quiz, accidentally preserved on the same tape.

title: Countdown to Christmas Begins
synopsis: The Super Family kicks off its battle-free Christmas special with everyday morning routines: breakfast, mask painting, and Stacy getting help with her Chinese homework from Nakama. Between gift-planning chatter and a parade of babies needing baths and snacks, the household settles into cozy holiday-prep mode.

title: Pineapple Pie and Days-Before-Christmas Math
synopsis: The family gathers for a chaotic holiday dinner, complete with a rambling bedtime-style story about a skyscraper family, a spread of pineapple pie and "cookie delight," and a running joke about exactly how many days before Christmas it actually is. Kids clamor for food while the parents wrangle plates, babies, and a growing crowd around the table.

title: Bath Time and Feather Duty
synopsis: It's bath night for the littlest Super Family members, with shampoo-versus-soap mixups and careful feather- and wing-brushing for the winged babies, plus a whirlpool tub that gets shut off mid-soak. Once everyone's clean and tucked in, the parents wind down and plan a sledding trip for the next day.

title: The Great Christmas Shopping Spree
synopsis: Morning coffee banter turns into an epic, increasingly absurd Christmas shopping trip: the parents debate telescopes, rocking chairs, and a mini tree before their gift list balloons past the 900th item. The spree spirals into daydreaming about a small fleet of new minivans, and maybe a Viper, just to haul all the presents home.

title: Toa Upgrades and a Fleet of Punch Buggies
synopsis: The shopping spree keeps escalating with talk of dangerous "Toa Nuva upgrade" kits and a debate over how many new cars, mostly punch buggies, the family actually needs. Back home, Grandma Pikachu cooks up her radish shish kebab and a spicy "super soup" for a hilariously crowded family dinner table full of hungry kids.

title: Invisible Wrapping on Christmas Eve
synopsis: On Christmas Eve, the family debates skipping the tree this year and unveils a goofy gift-wrapping trick, an "invisible" coating that hides the presents inside plain-looking boxes. Amid dish-cleaning and bath-time chores, someone poses the earnest question: does everyone actually know what Christmas is really about?

title: Tidying Up Before the Big Day
synopsis: A brief, low-key stretch of holiday tidying and quiet chatter, with a passing mention of getting a computer for Blossom as the kids help clear away the mess. Mostly light housekeeping talk with little narrated action.

title: Christmas Dinner, Dance, and the Sign-Off
synopsis: The family says grace, digs into the "famous soup," and closes out the night with an impromptu dance before cleaning up, though they note wistfully that the Toa never came home to get their Christmas present. The narrator formally wraps the sixth movie, jokes about his uncomfortable costume, and rattles off a list of camcorder effects and a mysterious 1999 side-project called "Doctor Senior 2000" before the tape drifts into chatter about an upcoming Pokemon-themed party with Crash, Coco, Spyro, and Meg.

title: Goldilocks and the Pee-Pee Dinner
synopsis: The kids act out a toy-and-Pokemon version of "Goldilocks and the Three Bears," complete with porridge, chairs, and beds, while also planning that night's dinner, jokingly dubbed the "pee-pee dinner" after a Pikachu gag. Everyone gets ready for guests, with Crash expected to be the first to arrive around 7:30.

title: Back After These Messages
synopsis: A goofy fake commercial break interrupts the action before returning to reheated pizza, Pikachu antics, and a running debate over what's appropriate for little Pikachu to watch on TV. Casual, low-key household chatter fills most of this stretch, with little else happening.

title: Pokemon Pancakes and Almost-Fireworks
synopsis: A scattered morning of silly mishaps: someone nearly blows a hole in the roof with a firework mix-up, breakfast turns into a running "Pokemon pancake" joke, and the household counts down to that evening's party, still set for 5:30.

title: Building a Snowmobile with Lego Pikachu
synopsis: Pikachu tinkers with a homemade snowmobile while the kids build Lego versions of Pikachu and an otter, plus a helicopter landing pad, in between a Pokemon-school day and hair-combing. The party countdown continues, now pegged at 5:45, as guests like Miss Coco start showing up.

title: Frosting, Vitamins, and a Half-Eaten Cake
synopsis: The party is in full swing: dishes get washed, treats get passed around, and the half-eaten cake gets topped with frosting and jelly for the kids. Amid the sugar rush there's a running gag about whether Pikachu got its vitamins, and someone brings up a mysterious "Fort Discovery."

title: The Puppy Cameo
synopsis: A brief, meandering wind-down after the party: more jelly jokes, a stray question about massage, and someone wondering what's next, before the camera catches a passing puppy and someone offers a cheerful hello to close things out.
